chapter: From Pittsburgh to Maxine Sullivan: management and style
title: The Cotton Club and Broadway with Louis Armstrong
summary: After 'Going Places' she joined the Cotton Club and a Broadway show; she enjoyed working with Louis.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Maybe we should mention also that you appeared in the Cotton Club, you have mentioned before.
And for a short time on the Broadway Stage. That was in '39?

Well, that's right. See, after I did the movie 'Going Places' in which Louie Armstrong and I appeared, there was a relationship between me and Louie because we went into the Cotton Club together and when they decided to do 'Swinging the Dream' we wound up as co-stars along with Benny Goodman in the band, and all the other acts. And Louie Armstrong and I were the last acts to play at the Cotton Club. And I don't recall having worked with Louie again after that.
So you have those three experiences.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

Well, let me see. Although we worked together we weren't that close. I didn't hang out with Louie and Louie didn't hang out with me. In the show we had a scene together and in the Cotton Club we had several numbers together. And then in the movie there was one or two scenes where we were together. So there was no, you know, no real crazy friendships there. I never knew Louie that well. We was just working in the same place.
Was it good to work with him?
Yes, of course. Well, I always enjoyed Louie. I loved his trumpet playing, you know. He was a very good musician as everybody knows, I mean, I don't have to say that.
